question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: The result is the input with every occurrence of a character in ESCAPES replaced by its replacement from that table, judged one code unit at a time with no context. Every other code unit is copied unchanged and in its original position.

The percent sign is itself escaped, and replacements are never re-examined: an input that already contains an escape sequence ("%3A") is escaped again ("%253A"), so the operation is NOT idempotent and the runner's single unescape restores the original exactly.
Carriage return and line feed are escaped independently: CRLF -> "%0D%0A", LF CR -> "%0A%0D".

The equals sign, semicolon, quotes, backslash, solidus, space, tab, every other control character (NUL, VT, FF, NEL, U+2028, U+2029), the fullwidth colon and comma (U+FF1A, U+FF0C), every non-ASCII letter and astral characters are copied unchanged. CITED FIDELITY package — the escaped set is exactly ESCAPES, the same set as @actions/core@3.0.1.
